Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As part of our onboarding review we need two things to close our privacy checklist for Redwood's processing of Globex customer data:

1) An evidence sampling approach that shows how you validate subprocessors' controls (SOC2 / ISO / manual evidence). For our audit we typically accept a random sample + targeted high-risk sample — we want to understand your methodology and a short example.

2) A retention map for each subprocessor that stores or transmits EU personal data (Art. 28 & 30 scope). The map should include: subprocessor name, location, data categories, retention period, and the legal basis for transfer.

Can you surface these as a short packet (PDF/CSV) and confirm whether you can provide an export of your Art.30 ledger or an excerpt covering the processors touching payment and identity flows?

We aim to complete this review by EOD Friday — would appreciate an ETA and any constraints.

Best,
Marta

Hi Marta / Irene — looping in a couple of clarifications from the privacy team after reviewing the initial stub:

1) Scope: We'll produce an Art.30 ledger excerpt limited to processors that handle payments, identity resolution, and customer PII. That will keep the export narrow and redacted where appropriate.

2) Sample size: For the random component we default to 10% of active processors (min 5, max 25) over the past 12 months; for targeted we'll include all processors with high transfer risk or lacking a recent attestation. Confirm if Globex requires a different minimum.

3) Evidence types: we can supply one of the following per sampled processor: SOC2 report (PDF stub), ISO cert summary (PDF), or attestation emails. Where the subprocessor refuses external sharing we provide an internal control narrative and screenshots.

4) DPIA note: If you intend to use the ledger to update your DPIA, please confirm which processing operations to map — payments/identity/analytics — so we attach the appropriate data flow extracts.

I'm attaching art30_ledger_excerpt.csv (redacted rows) as an example record format.

Thanks,
